anxiety noun

also worry, worries, nervousness, worry (someone), worry (be anxious), anxiously

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.18: sollicitūdō aegritūdō cum cōgitātiōne (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Phorm. 4.1.22
Traupman 409 (worry)
Traupman 159

sollicitūdō, sollicitūdinis f.

noun, third declension

worry, anxiety

The common word for worry and care, in Terence and Cicero alike, singular or plural.

Other words

  • ānxietās, ānxietātis f. — anxiety as a cast of mind

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.27; Juv. 13.211 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 272; Andresian p. 36

    Cicero’s word for a lasting anxiousness, against angor, a moment’s anguish (Lewis & Short). Long ā before -nx-.

  • cūra, cūrae f. — care, worry (about something)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 149: cūra + gen.; Traupman 159

  • sollicitō, sollicitāre, sollicitāvī, sollicitātum — to worry, trouble (someone)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 159

  • sollicitor, sollicitārī — to worry, be anxious

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Traupman 159

    The passive of sollicitāre, “be troubled”.

  • ānxiē — anxiously

    adverb · also used · classical · Traupman 272

See also anxious, concern.
